elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: New Subparagraph 27.2: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York." The original document selected no law at all (old 27.2 only instructed courts to disregard law-identifying facts), so this is an express and unconditional choice within the accepted set.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: New 27.2 second sentence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute arising under this Agreement." Both court tiers and the New York County anchor are present, and the competing mechanic is cured: 27.1 no longer lets the Management Committee "determine the method, such as arbitration" and no longer states that the procedure is the "sole and exclusive remedy," with the added sentence confirming the escalation "shall not limit any Party's recourse to the courts designated in Subparagraph 27.2."

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not a defect: the drafter elected the preferred level, and the fallback is offered only in the margin comment.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: The forum designated is the state and federal courts in New York County, so no Delaware/California/London forum appears. Consistent with the preferred election.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: both preferred elements are met in operative language (express New York choice of law plus unconditional exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County). No conditional trigger or undefined term supports either element.

The clause was effectively a missing governing-law/venue clause: old 27.2 selected no law and instead told "all courts and tribunals wherever situated" to ignore law-identifying facts. A concise replacement of that subparagraph with the choice-of-law and venue sentences is minimal for a missing clause, and the deleted fact-exclusion language becomes inoperative once an express choice exists, so nothing favourable to us is surrendered.

The edit to 27.1 is necessary, not an extra: under the playbook an exclusive-jurisdiction result is not achieved while a competing route survives, and the original 27.1 made the Management Committee procedure (which could impose "arbitration") the "sole and exclusive remedy." Striking the method-selection/arbitration option and the exclusivity sentence, plus the short conforming sentence preserving court recourse, is the least change needed to make 27.2 operative.

Unrelated mechanics survive intact: the reasonable-efforts obligation, the Management Committee escalation itself, and the sentence requiring continued performance during any dispute are all retained. The cross-reference "courts designated in Subparagraph 27.2" resolves to the newly drafted courts sentence, so there is no dangling reference.

Action item for the drafter (outside this checklist, not a defect in the rendered text): the rationale notes Paragraph 20 presupposes arbitration in an unspecified country. That paragraph was not supplied for inspection; if it contains an operative arbitration or alternative-forum mechanic, it must be conformed or the exclusive-jurisdiction sentence in 27.2 will be contradicted elsewhere in the document.
Tone and comment comply: concise, first person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the Delaware/California/England-and-Wales fallback without lecturing.
